chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibn Mihzam, from Talhah ibn Zayd, who said:
"The hamīl is not given inheritance except with clear proof."
He said: "The hamīl is one whom a woman brings while pregnant, having been taken captive while she was pregnant; then afterward his father or his brother recognizes him by that."

key_terms.أَبُوهُ أَوْ أَخُوهُ: The father or brother whose recognition is mentioned as part of establishing the child’s identity.
key_terms.الْحَمِيلُ: A child whose lineage is claimed in the context described by the hadith, especially regarding inheritance.
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ حُبْلَى: A pregnant woman, central to the legal scenario described.
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٍ: Clear legal proof or evidence required to establish the inheritance claim.
key_terms.سُبِيَتْ: Was taken captive; this defines the circumstance in which the child’s status is discussed.

ai.seo_question: When does a child of a pregnant captive woman inherit in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the inheritance of a child identified through the circumstance of a pregnant captive woman. It states that such inheritance is not established unless there is clear evidence, and the Imam عليه السلام clarifies what is meant by al-hamīl in this context.
